title: Ordering at a café
context: You are at a café counter.

n1.speaker: Barista
n1.say: Hi! What can I get you?

choices.feedback: This sounds rude. Use 'I'd like...' or 'Could I have...'.

n2.speaker: Barista
n2.say: Sure. Would you like anything else?

choices.feedback: Good. You added a request politely.
Too abrupt. Try 'Sorry, could you repeat that?'

end.speaker: Barista
end.say: Great, I'll have that ready for you in a moment.

title: Job interview basics
context: You are at the start of a job interview for a customer service role.

n1.speaker: Interviewer
n1.say: Tell me a little about yourself.

choices.text: I have three years of experience in customer service, and I enjoy helping people.
I am a person who likes things.
choices.feedback: Too vague. Mention your experience and strengths.

choices.text: I don't know what to say.
choices.feedback: Prepare a short answer about your work and skills in advance.

n2.speaker: Interviewer
n2.say: Why do you want this job?

choices.text: I like the company's focus on training, and I want to grow my skills.
choices.feedback: It links your goals to the employer.
Honest, but add a reason related to the role.
It may be true, but focus on what you can offer.

n3.speaker: Interviewer
n3.say: Do you have any questions for us?

choices.text: Yes, what does a typical day look like in this role?

choices.feedback: Acceptable, but a question shows you are engaged.

end.speaker: Interviewer
end.say: Thank you. We'll be in touch soon.
